```{r}
#| label: map-region
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
library(readr); library(dplyr); library(leaflet); library(htmltools)

region <- read_csv("data/region.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(!is.na(lat), !is.na(lon))

# Marcadores desenhados como SVG: a forma carrega o papel do ponto, e a
# distinção sobrevive a impressão em preto e branco.
marker_svg <- function(role) {
  col <- c(sampling = "#1d7a73", support = "#b08b3e", city = "#26343a")[role]
  shape <- switch(role,
    sampling = '<circle cx="14" cy="14" r="8"',
    support  = '<rect x="6" y="6" width="16" height="16" rx="2"',
    city     = '<polygon points="14,5 23,22 5,22"')
  svg <- sprintf('<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="28" height="28">%s fill="%s" fill-opacity="0.85" stroke="white" stroke-width="2"/></svg>',
                 shape, col)
  # data URI com o SVG percent-encoded: evita depender de base64enc
  paste0("data:image/svg+xml;charset=UTF-8,", utils::URLencode(svg, reserved = TRUE))
}

# Bacia (opcional): largue um .gpkg ou .shp em data/gis/ e a camada entra
# sozinha; sem arquivo, o mapa sai só com os pontos.
basin_file <- list.files("data/gis", pattern = "\\.(gpkg|shp)$", full.names = TRUE)
basin <- if (length(basin_file) && requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE)) {
  sf::st_transform(sf::st_read(basin_file[1], quiet = TRUE), 4326)
} else NULL

if (nrow(region) == 0) {
  HTML('<p><em>Sem coordenadas em <code>data/region.csv</code>.</em></p>')
} else {
  region$icon_url <- vapply(region$role, marker_svg, character(1))

  legend_html <- paste0(
    '<div style="background:rgba(255,255,255,.9);padding:8px 10px;',
    'border-radius:5px;font-size:12px;line-height:1.7">',
    '<span style="display:inline-block;width:12px;height:12px;border-radius:50%;',
    'background:#1d7a73"></span>&nbsp; Sampling site<br>',
    '<span style="display:inline-block;width:12px;height:12px;',
    'background:#b08b3e"></span>&nbsp; Logistical support<br>',
    '<span style="display:inline-block;width:0;height:0;border-left:7px solid transparent;',
    'border-right:7px solid transparent;border-bottom:12px solid #26343a"></span>&nbsp; City',
    '</div>')

  m <- leaflet(region, height = 440,
               options = leafletOptions(scrollWheelZoom = FALSE)) |>
    addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldImagery", group = "Satellite") |>
    addProviderTiles("CartoDB.Positron",  group = "Map")

  if (!is.null(basin)) {
    m <- addPolygons(m, data = basin, fill = TRUE, fillColor = "#1d7a73",
                     fillOpacity = 0.12, color = "#1d7a73", weight = 2,
                     group = "Basin")
  }

  # Uma chamada por papel: rótulos de pontos vizinhos (UFMT e Cuiabá ficam a
  # 4 km) saem para lados opostos em vez de se sobrepor.
  dirs <- c(sampling = "right", support = "right", city = "left")
  for (r in unique(region$role)) {
    d <- region[region$role == r, ]
    m <- addMarkers(
      m, data = d, lng = ~lon, lat = ~lat,
      icon = icons(iconUrl = d$icon_url, iconWidth = 26, iconHeight = 26,
                   iconAnchorX = 13, iconAnchorY = 13),
      label = ~place,
      labelOptions = labelOptions(noHide = TRUE, direction = dirs[[r]],
                                  textsize = "13px", opacity = 0.9),
      popup = ~paste0("<b>", place, "</b><br>", note))
  }

  # Moldura proporcional à extensão dos pontos, não um valor fixo em graus.
  pad_y <- max(0.08, diff(range(region$lat)) * 0.12)
  pad_x <- max(0.08, diff(range(region$lon)) * 0.12)

  m |>
    addControl(HTML(legend_html), position = "topright") |>
    addScaleBar("bottomleft") |>
    addLayersControl(baseGroups = c("Satellite", "Map"),
                     overlayGroups = if (!is.null(basin)) "Basin" else NULL,
                     options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = TRUE)) |>
    fitBounds(min(region$lon) - pad_x, min(region$lat) - pad_y,
              max(region$lon) + pad_x, max(region$lat) + pad_y)
}
```

::: {.figure-caption}
My study area in region of Mato Grosso, Brazil. Circles are sampling sites area,
squares are logistical support (field station and laboratory), the triangle is
the state capital. 
:::
